named_minor_fixes.old: There is identifiable cross-border allocation evidence in Reuters' report on Chinese investors moving toward offshore assets and the associated Hong Kong wealth inflows. That should not be relabeled as buying Hong Kong equities or any particular sector. Similarly, Reuters describes growing Indian mutual-fund assets, but assets under management combine several influences and do not identify a universal marginal buyer for global stocks. The useful portfolio distinction is between a reported allocation channel and an inferred destination. Both stories suggest active demand for investment vehicles; neither justifies claiming that every regional market is receiving fresh equity inflows. [[n0300]] [[n1570]]
named_minor_fixes.new: Reuters reports Chinese investors seeking offshore assets and increased Hong Kong wealth inflows. That allocation can support wealth services without identifying a purchase of Hong Kong equities or any particular sector. Reuters also reports growing Indian mutual-fund assets. Fund assets can change through market valuation as well as subscriptions and withdrawals, so their size alone cannot identify the marginal buyer of global stocks. Keep the portfolio tied to a confirmed commercial channel rather than assume a universal wave of equity purchases. Cross-border diversification and domestic fund growth can benefit different intermediaries, with the eventual earnings dependent on customer activity and costs. [[n0300]] [[n1570]]
